parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the need for a pure Node.js ESM .mjs port, manual argparse-compatible parsing, exact stdout/stderr/status behavior, no external modules, and a split library under /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created local tracking tasks for Python compat, argparse, networkx, entry point, and verification, wrote the implementation itself, and delegated only late verifier/reviewer work to a workflow.
parallel.implementation: The parent implemented Python int/repr/argv/io/textwrap helpers, an argparse subset, Graph/DiGraph/DAG modules, hashing utilities, and /output/test5.mjs, then made cleanup fixes to textwrap and argv.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All generated files were placed under /output and artifact validation listed test5.mjs plus the local library modules as OK; the final response file is empty because the process timed out.
parallel.verification: The run probed the reference executable, smoke-tested the Node port, ran an independent DAG oracle and syntax/import audit, then launched a nine-agent verifier workflow that never returned before the final spot-check was killed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation passed all 162 samples, but the in-trajectory verifier workflow was killed with result null, task 5 remained unfinished, and the parent ended on Exit 137 rather than a completed closure report.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual argparse parity, DAG behavior, no external dependencies, and /output delivery requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: With workflows and delegation disabled, the single parent actor owned probing, implementation, differential testing, fixes, and final artifact delivery.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote a compact cli parser/help layer, Python builtins/unicode helpers, networkx digraph/DAG modules, and /output/test5.mjs, then fixed Unicode negative-option and usage wrapping behavior discovered by difftests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial placed all artifacts in /output, and artifact validation found test5.mjs and the expected local library files with no delegation contamination.
serial.verification: Serial ran executable probes, a differential harness, symlinked program-name checks, and reran difftests after fixes; the last rerun was killed by timeout, but official evaluation passed 162/162.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial final response is empty and the last local difftest was killed at timeout, but no child results were outstanding and the official evaluator accepted the artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, .mjs, manual argv, no-dependency, /output, and networkx DAG equivalence requirements and probed executable behavior before coding.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and independently probed executable behavior for DAG, argparse, Unicode integer, repr, help, and stream behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference explains outcome; both delivered artifacts that the official evaluator accepted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used parent-owned TaskCreate tracking for Python compat, argparse, networkx, entry point, and verification, then delegated verification to a workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows disabled and completed the probing, implementation, differential harness, fixes, and checks in the single parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child verifier pool while serial retained one-owner control; implementation ownership itself was present in both runs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The verifier workflow gave children the harness, port paths, constraints, and topic-specific audit briefs, with instructions to report only demonstrated findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial avoided cross-agent interfaces; the same actor observed reference behavior, edited files, and interpreted difftest results directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child handoff and shared-workspace context boundaries; serial did not need child interface contracts or handoff reduction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a larger hierarchy under lib/python, lib/argparse, and lib/networkx/classes/utils, then edited textwrap and argv after smoke checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a smaller hierarchy under lib/cli, lib/python, and lib/networkx, then edited parser/help code after local differential mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The code organization and fix sequence differed, but both produced functionally sufficient ESM artifacts for the official cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched the verifier workflow in the background and never received an aggregate result because the workflow status became killed with result null.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification results were local command results in the parent trajectory; no child result retrieval or join was required.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the lifecycle of delegated verifier results; serial had no delegated result lifecycle, only a final local command killed at timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent kept modifying /output while verifier children were active, but children were instructed not to write /output and no concrete write collision is shown.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made all artifact writes and edits directly in the parent trajectory, with no observed delegation or concurrent shared-state writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created shared read/verification state around live child agents, while serial preserved a single-writer artifact history.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran smoke tests, an independent DAG oracle, syntax/import checks, and launched the verifier workflow; official evaluation later passed 162/162.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a local differential harness, used mismatches to fix argparse and help layout behavior, and official evaluation later passed 162/162.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had enough delivered behavior for the evaluator, but parallel intended broad verifier did not close while serial observed fixes stayed in the parent loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one workflow with nine verifier agents near the end of a timed-out run; workflow state is killed and the parent final spot-check exits 137.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also hit the outer timeout after a final local difftest rerun, but had no subagent budget or workflow result to join.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel closure risk is specifically the late broad verifier fan-out; the serial timeout is an ordinary single-trajectory closure timeout after local fixes.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations show both parallel and serial passed 162/162, so there is no discordant official outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is the verification and closure strategy: parallel used a late nine-agent verifier workflow that was killed without an aggregate result, while serial kept differential testing and fixes in the parent trajectory. Both artifacts were nevertheless acceptable to the official evaluator.
parallel_contributors: Parent-built modular implementation passed official evaluation.
Late verifier fan-out left in-trajectory verification unfinished but did not prevent artifact success.
serial_contributors: Single parent trajectory fixed observed argparse/help mismatches locally.
No delegation or child-result lifecycle was introduced.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two solutions used different module layouts and helper naming, but both satisfied the official executable comparisons.
Both processes timed out and produced empty final responses, so process timeout alone is not an outcome discriminator.
evaluator_effects: Official evaluator judged delivered artifacts rather than final response text, so both timed-out processes still received passing solution outcomes.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained label is a parallel adverse process pattern only
